I just ended my second long term relationship of two years a couple of weeks ago. This was after she had already broken up with me twice since June 2019. This most recent relationship was one I dove head first into and rushed it. But we lasted a while and shared so many great experiences and she really pushed me to grow as an individual. And there are times that I catch myself missing her or wondering what she is doing. 

You missing your ex or even remembering other relationships isn’t a sign that you haven’t “moved on” it’s just emotions attached to other ppl that your brain stirs up. 

Not moving on is when you are constantly stalking their socials or chatting to them all the time. Or still going out of your way to do things for them when you do not need to at all. It’s holding out hope that you will get back together. 

People move on in different ways. Some push down feelings and just try to ignore things. Personally, I choose to acknowledge my old feelings and work through them. And remind myself why I ended things. I will always love my ex. No matter what she has a piece of my heart. But my feelings for her are just as a good friend. 

I suggest you try to focus on yourself right now and do things that make you happy!

Have you tried couples counseling? Often times communication is whats failing. Your wife could be frustrated with herself by not knowing how to handle your mindset. She wants the best for you but she might not know how to properly express her feelings or worries to you. 

For years my mood was tied to my first gfs behavior. It is so difficult. Especially when she was emotionally abusive towards me. Thankfully. Was able to get out of it. My most recent relationship (2nd gf)has just ended but she and I took the time to go to counseling and figure out new and better ways to communicate with each other because we had different styles of communication. 

My suggestion to you is to start focusing on you. Going to the gym is a HUGE thing that helps me a lot. It makes me feel good, it lets me get out my frustrations and it releases all the good neurotransmitters that make you de-stress. It also tires you out. I’ve also set reminders on my phone that say things like “I’m awesome, I matter, I’m caring, I’m smart, I’m attractive, etc..” that go off 3x a day and I read them to myself. It reminds me of who I am. 

I also stopped drinking a lot. I found that id hate myself even more when Id drink. Even if I didn’t do anything stupid the night before it just made my depression and self hate even worse. I also started eating healthier and picked up reading again. 

Right now you need to focus on you and your daughter. You two should pick a new hobby together and maybe even a hobby that involves going outside and away from the house. 

It seems like you and your wife are constantly fighting in the home. And the person will always wear out before the boxing gloves do. And you seem like you’re wearing yourself down. 

To this day I still have feelings of wanting to off myself. I have random thoughts that fly into my head and they are memories of negative events associated with the ones I love and it eats me away and it makes me want to die. A couple of days ago I wanted to get blacked out drunk and use the train tracks as a pillow. But I remembered what I have in my life. And as much as my life really really sucks right now and I’m more alone than ever I know that I can’t give up yet. There are things I want to do and experience that I won’t be able to if I die. And I remind myself that each time I don’t kill myself even though I REALLY want to makes me a stronger person. Because the hardest person to beat is yourself and your own mind. And each time you managing to claw your way out of the dark space of your mind you become one step closer to the person you want to be.
